full_judgment: 16. Adoption of a procedure which is positively prohibited by the Cr.P.C. Where the defect has occasioned an injustice in the sense that the accused were embarrassed in their defence in having to meet a multifarious accumulation of evidence upon a diversity of Counts, several of which were illegally joined in the trial, such defect cannot be cured by section 537 Cr.P.C. and the trial is illegal. It is held in the decision reported in 10 D.L.R. (S.C) 29 that joint trial held on the offences charged not committed within the same transaction is illegal and not curable under section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Whether joint trial is illegal or irregular, the test is whether accused has been prejudiced by such trial or not, and whether there occasioned any failure of justice by holding such trial. If prejudice is caused by occasioning failure of justice, such trial is positively illegal. In the instant case we have seen that the occurrence took place on 1.3.75 and the trial started on 18.8.84, and concluded on 9th December, 1984 taking a long period of about 9 years and the accused appellants had to face a number of charges in place of one and they appeared to have been bewildered and embarrassed in having to defend themselves against such numerous charges. This illegal joinder of charges which did not form part of the same transaction, in the facts and circumstances of the case, leads to a clear presumption of prejudice caused to the accused appellants occasioning failure of justice. So we find from the aforesaid decisions that the trial of the accused appellants and others having been concluded by misjoinder of charges prohibited by law which in our opinion is illegal and the trial is vitiated thereby.
